sections.h2: How a house changes hands in Burbank
sections.html:
Most Burbank houses sell by listing, by a private deal between neighbors or relatives, or to an investor who pays cash. Residents here tend to stay: 80.9 percent of homes are occupied by their owners, and 92.9 percent of residents had not moved in the past year.

That low turnover shapes a sale. Long-time owners often put off a new roof, a furnace or rewiring, so a buyer's inspector may produce a long list. A seller facing that list can fix items before listing, offer a credit, or hand the house to a buyer who expects to do the work. Whichever path you take, the City Clerk and the Cook County recording office are on the route to closing.

Burbank is a Cook County city in Stickney Township, ZIP code 60459. The latest population estimate is 28,578, which is 3.0 percent below the 2020 base. The typical home value is $275,700 for 2020 through 2024 across 9,539 households, typical gross rent is $1,265, middle household income is $80,116, and the one-way commute is 31.3 minutes.

Most of the area was built out after 1950, so a typical house is now about seven decades old. Buyers' first questions concern roofs, furnaces and plumbing. Pace buses link the city with the southwest side of Chicago and the south suburbs.

sections.h2: Transfer tax at the City Clerk
sections.html:
Burbank taxes the transfer of a house. The City Clerk's page posts a two-part transfer tax form, refreshed in 2024, and the office at 6530 W 79th Street processes it. Phone 708-599-5500 before closing to confirm the rate, who pays and which transfers are exempt.

The clerk works weekdays, closing at 5 p.m. on Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday and at 6 p.m. on Tuesday. The office is closed on weekends. The city posts its 2026 closure dates, which include the Friday after Thanksgiving, so plan the stamp pickup around them.

The state's separate levy is collected through the county recorder, and the Illinois Department of Revenue's PTAX-203 declaration goes in with the deed at recording.

sections.h2: Repairs that need a city permit
sections.html:
The Building Department at City Hall decides whether a project needs a permit. It calls for one on new construction and on structural, ventilation, exit, plumbing, electrical and fire-safety changes. The city's page lists many everyday jobs.

  • Roof recoating or replacement, siding, gutters and masonry.
  • Fences, driveways, porches, sheds and garages.
  • Furnaces, air conditioning and boilers.
  • Any remodel, plus demolition of a structure.

Every contractor who works in Burbank has to meet the city's contractor requirements, and swapping a gas water heater earns a no-charge inspection of venting, safety valve and connections. The office answers at 708-599-5500, option 2.

A buyer's attorney will ask whether past work was permitted. An unpermitted change can slow a conventional sale, which is why some owners choose a buyer who accepts the house with those questions open.

sections.h2: Paperwork to line up before closing
sections.html:
The title company or attorney usually runs the process, but only you can supply the permit history and confirm who owns the property of record.

Burbank seller paperwork
DocumentWhere it comes from
DeedYour records, so the clerk and recorder can match the owners
PTAX-203 declarationSigned by both sides
Transfer tax formThe City Clerk's page
Permit recordsAny roof, furnace, electrical or plumbing job
Tax billYour latest Cook County bill

Exemptions show up as deductions on the second installment bill. If you cannot tell whether a homeowner or senior exemption is in place, ask the Assessor or the Treasurer before closing, because it shifts the proration on the settlement statement.

The recording office run by the Cook County Clerk keeps hours of 9 to 5, accepts its last customer at 4:45 and offers a legal help desk staffed by volunteer attorneys.

The Building Commissioner's office handles permit reviews, property maintenance and code enforcement, along with variance and zoning requests. Call 708-599-5500, option 2, with questions about your address, and ask for the permit and violation history in writing if you can.

If your house has an open violation, resolve it before the contract is signed. A title search or a buyer's inspection can surface it, and an unresolved item can stall a closing or cost you leverage in a price talk.

Emptying a house after an inheritance or a move often starts with a sale of the contents, and Burbank regulates those. Garage sales need a permit from the Building Department, are barred on Sundays and are capped at two per year. Guidelines and fees are available at 708-599-5500, option 2.

Plan the cleanout dates with that cap in mind, since an owner who held two sales earlier in the year cannot hold a third. Anything left over can go with a hauler before the final walkthrough. If the house is going to a cash buyer who accepts it with contents in place, ask for that in the contract so nobody has to haul anything.

Of residents, 51.1 percent are Hispanic or Latino, and 60.9 percent of residents age 5 and over speak another language at home. A listing with Spanish-language materials, or a translator at showings, reaches households a one-language flyer would miss.

The mix includes young families and long-settled older owners. Yard and school access speak to the first group, and single-floor living and easy maintenance speak to the second.

A Burbank sale usually runs in this order. Your title company or attorney opens the file and orders the title search. You and the buyer sign the PTAX-203. Someone picks up the city transfer tax form from the clerk's page and brings it to the office with the deed, after a phone call to confirm the rate and who pays. The Cook County Clerk records the deed, and the state's levy is collected at that step.

Call the Building Department before you list if you remember work on the roof, furnace or plumbing. Finding out about an unclosed permit in week one of a contract is much worse than finding out in week one of your listing.

A cash buyer does not wait on a lender's appraisal or underwriting, so the closing date is easier to hold. The clerk's transfer form, the PTAX-203 and the recording step still apply, and so does the question of open permits. Compare offers by what you net after repairs, not by the headline number.

faqs.q: Where do I find Burbank transfer tax forms?
faqs.a: On the City Clerk's page at burbankil.gov, where the two-page form was updated in 2024, or at the clerk's office, 6530 W 79th Street. Call 708-599-5500 to confirm what to bring.

faqs.q: When is the Burbank clerk's office open?
faqs.a: Weekdays, with Tuesday running to 6 p.m. and the other weekdays closing at 5 p.m. The office is shut on weekends and on the closure dates the city posts.

faqs.q: Which county records a Burbank deed?
faqs.a: Cook County, through its Clerk's recording office, which takes customers from 9 a.m. until 4:45 p.m.

faqs.q: Is a permit required for re-roofing in Burbank?
faqs.a: Yes. The Building Department names roof replacement among the work that needs a permit. Phone 708-599-5500, option 2, to confirm the steps for your address.

faqs.q: Can a Burbank house with repair problems be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers routinely take houses in their present state. Collect permit records, ask the Building Department about anything open, and compare offers by what you net after repairs.
